emerging_technology: Agentic AI built on large language models (LLM-based agents that plan, use tools, and complete multi-step tasks)
intended_application: Proposed bounded applicant-support workflow: retrieve approved program information, ask clarifying questions, plan next steps, and request a counselor appointment through a permission-limited tool. Staff approve outbound messages and any record changes. Excludes admission, scholarship, visa and eligibility decisions.
organization: NYU School of Professional Studies (SPS) - graduate admissions
industry_sector: Higher education - graduate and professional admissions and recruitment (United States). International applicants include EU residents; exact legal obligations require specialist review.
business_need: Know where agent-based applicant support sits in today's landscape and which external developments should change the staged path (proof of concept, then a gated bounded experiment) or its vendor and design requirements.
users_stakeholders: Prospective students; admissions counselors; SPS enrollment management leadership (sponsor); marketing/enrollment staff; NYU IT and SPS technology staff (platforms and vendors); NYU privacy and compliance officers
adoption_posture: Moderate / fast-follower (held constant across all cases; for NYU SPS this is a course-case assumption, not an official policy).
capabilities_constraints: Verified: the SPS graduate application site offers a virtual assistant named Violet (D49, 2026-11-15); NYU Admissions runs a generative-AI admissions bot with live-agent hand-off (D17). The platform behind Violet and SPS's CRM is not named in public sources (D49). No vendor has been selected. Readiness (C6): proof of concept ready with conditions; live experiment not yet ready.
risk_consequence_context: Wrong deadlines or promises can harm applicants, and the organization is accountable for what its agent says; unauthorized actions can expose data. No applicant records are used in this assignment. No legal determination is made.
management_question: Where does agent-based applicant support sit in the current technology landscape, which development matters most for NYU SPS over the next 12 months, and what signal should trigger a reassessment?
time_horizon: 12 months: proof of concept this term; bounded-experiment decision within this admissions cycle
additional_context: Upstream: the Adoption specialist (C4) classifies agent-based applicant support as bleeding edge and permits a proof of concept now, gated to a bounded experiment; the Readiness specialist (C6) finds the proof of concept ready with conditions and the live experiment not yet ready, and asks Landscape to shortlist vendors only against data-terms requirements (no-training, retention, deletion, least-privilege connector).
